title: Site-independent storage from multi-day weather through seasonal imbalance

concept.text: The proposed innovation is electricity storage that can be deployed across many regions without unusual geology and can economically bridge both prolonged renewable-generation shortfalls and seasonal differences between electricity supply and demand. It would combine adequate electricity-to-electricity efficiency, durable operation, widely available materials and sufficiently low total cost to support replacement of fossil firm capacity. The advance is the combination of these capabilities at practical scale; demonstrating one of them does not establish the complete capability.

Three different time requirements matter. Discharge duration describes how long a charged installation can supply a specified power output. Retention describes how long energy can remain stored before delivery, including losses and energy used to keep the installation ready. Seasonal balancing requires enough retained energy, charging opportunities and delivery capacity to address the actual seasonal mismatch in a regional electricity system. A 100-hour discharge demonstration therefore would not, by itself, demonstrate seasonal balancing.

Site independence means broad siting flexibility rather than literal suitability at every location. Pumped-storage hydropower and cavern-based compressed-air storage illustrate why this distinction matters: DOE's August 2024 assessment identifies geological constraints for these technologies. A broadly deployable alternative would still need practical sites, grid connections and other infrastructure, with its remaining constraints documented.

significance.text: A grid must continuously balance generation, demand, losses and exchanges with storage. Its transient stores of energy do not provide the bulk reserves needed for multi-day or seasonal balancing. Storage can hold energy through electrochemical, chemical, thermal, mechanical and other physical mechanisms, including flywheels. The potentially revolutionary capability is to make much larger quantities of electricity available for later use across the required intervals, wherever the system needs them. DOE identifies shifting clean generation into periods when generation is unavailable or insufficient as a central purpose of cheaper storage.

Conditional system-level synthesis: if storage and its charging resources were adequately sized, surplus wind and solar production could supply later shortfalls, potentially reducing dependence on fossil reserve capacity and the amount of generation overbuilding needed for reliability. The magnitude of those benefits would depend on regional weather, demand, transmission, charging availability, reliability requirements and economics. Storage shifts available energy; it does not create the energy needed to cover a sustained deficit.

The analogy to making electricity a stockpileable commodity has limits. Electricity is already stored in several forms; the proposed change is to make storage broadly deployable and economical across much longer balancing intervals. Charging and discharge power, retention losses and finite inventories would continue to constrain its usefulness. Solving stationary electricity storage would not itself solve industrial fuel production, hydrogen feedstock supply or the mass and energy-density requirements of aircraft batteries.

DOE's Storage Shot provides an overlapping cost ambition, not a definition of this broader innovation. Its January 2025 fact sheet specifies a 90% cost reduction from a 2020 lithium-ion baseline for systems delivering at least 10 hours within the decade. The August 2024 synthesis associates the initiative with a $0.05/kWh levelized cost of storage target. Neither statement establishes seasonal performance.

missing_breakthrough.text: The unresolved capability is a demonstrated combination of broad siting flexibility, multi-day delivery, seasonal retention and delivery, acceptable losses, durable operation, available materials and competitive system economics. The supplied evidence documents important barriers, but it does not establish that no technology anywhere meets this combination as of November 1, 2026. The concept remains a meaningful engineering objective without relying on that universal absence claim.

Cost is a documented barrier across the technology families assessed by DOE. Its August 2024 synthesis projects baseline 2030 levelized costs above the Storage Shot target. Geological requirements restrict pumped hydro and cavern-based compressed air, while lithium-ion applications described in that report typically provide services for 10 hours or less. That description of typical use is not a physical maximum discharge duration and does not establish that every longer-duration lithium-ion configuration is uneconomic. Likewise, the supplied review does not establish a general quantitative round-trip-efficiency failure for chemical carriers.

Engineering synthesis: a practical solution must make a large energy inventory affordable even when seasonal use produces relatively few complete cycles. It must also control losses during charging, storage and discharge, including auxiliary consumption; sustain the required output; and limit degradation and maintenance over its intended life. Efficiency should be judged alongside the cost and availability of charging energy and the full cost of delivered electricity. A single efficiency threshold cannot establish economic usefulness across all regional applications.

Engineering synthesis: scale introduces further requirements beyond a successful storage module. Materials and manufacturing must support the required deployment volume, plant performance must survive integration of many units, and siting flexibility must remain credible once land, infrastructure and operating requirements are included. Seasonal capability also requires evidence that retained energy can be recovered when needed, rather than an inference from a short-duration efficiency measurement.

current_state.text: DOE's January 2025 Long Duration Storage Shot fact sheet presents the 10+ hour, 90% cost reduction objective as a target for the decade. The associated $0.05/kWh figure in the August 2024 synthesis is a levelized cost of storage target, not an installed energy-capacity price. These dated documents do not report achievement of the full innovation and do not establish its subsequent attainment or nonattainment.

The August 2024 DOE synthesis projects baseline 2030 costs above its target across the assessed technologies. Using expert inputs and Monte Carlo modeling, it also identifies innovation portfolios that could bring pumped storage and compressed air below $0.05/kWh levelized cost of storage. Flow batteries approach that level: their detailed section reports $0.052–$0.057/kWh, slightly above the target despite broader summary language suggesting attainment. These are modeled outcomes for approximately 10-hour systems, not operating-fleet results or demonstrations of seasonal storage. Cost progress in a geology-dependent technology also does not establish broad siting flexibility.

The supplied research attributes a potentially relevant multi-day result to a California Energy Commission Energize Innovation project page: a Form Energy iron-air prototype module reportedly passed third-party tests in 2025 observed by the Electric Power Research Institute, including discharge exceeding 100 hours and a round-trip-efficiency check. The research says the page did not publish the measured efficiency. However, no retained page text or artifact accompanies that citation in the supplied evidence, so these details remain an attributed account that the validated review could not verify. That evidence gap does not establish that the reported tests did not occur.

The same unverified project-page account gives a module build target of about 3 kW and 3,000 kWh and describes applying the work toward a first utility-scale deployment of 1.5 MW and 150 MWh in Mendocino County. Those figures should remain identified as reported design or deployment targets, not measured operating performance. In particular, the module's stated power and energy values cannot be used to establish its tested discharge duration without clarification of their definitions and test conditions. The research lists a project term of June 30, 2020–December 31, 2025, reports a December 2025 conclusion and notes that the page header still displayed Active when consulted. Without retained page content, the relationship between those statements remains unresolved.

Even if the attributed module tests are confirmed, they would establish a narrower achievement than sustained operation of a plant at tens of megawatts with published efficiency, degradation and cost. Announced commercial projects and planned factories likewise do not establish those operating results. The supplied evidence does not establish completion of the proposed demonstration framework.

The supplied review reports complete retained text for the two DOE documents, but no retained content for the project page or the cited Utility Dive article. The independent DOE findings therefore do not depend on the secondary article, whose asserted publication date and account cannot be confirmed here. The supplied freshness record is empty, leaving subsequent demonstrations and the overall state of the field as of November 1, 2026 unresolved. This is a limit on the available account, not evidence that later progress is absent.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: operate a grid-connected plant at a scale of at least tens of megawatts, deliver at least 100 hours of discharge at a clearly specified output and repeat relevant operating cycles over at least one year. Publish electricity-to-electricity efficiency with a defined measurement boundary, auxiliary consumption, usable energy, output power, degradation, availability, maintenance and cost. These scale, duration and observation-period thresholds are proposed criteria for this record, not established standards. One year would provide initial operational evidence rather than prove lifetime durability.
completion_criteria.label: Grid-connected tens-of-megawatts plant demonstrates 100-hour discharge across year-long cycling

completion_criteria.text: Proposed seasonal demonstration: separately retain and deliver energy over the seasonal intervals required by the intended regional application. Report retention losses, standby consumption, recoverable energy and delivery performance after storage. A 100-hour discharge or retention across a few weeks alone would not establish seasonal balancing. The test must connect the plant's measured capabilities to the timing and magnitude of the regional mismatch it is intended to address.
completion_criteria.label: Seasonal energy delivery matches regional imbalance timing and magnitude

completion_criteria.text: Proposed system validation: use measured plant performance in an independent reliability and economic study of a region with high variable-renewable generation and no unusual geological advantage. Include realistic charging resources, weather variability, transmission constraints, required reserves and fully accounted costs. Demonstrate how much fossil firm capacity can be replaced while meeting the stated reliability requirement. Document material availability, manufacturing requirements and remaining siting constraints. Replication across multiple ordinary sites would strengthen the claim of broad deployability, while finite demonstrations would establish tested breadth rather than literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Independent regional study quantifies reliable fossil firm capacity replacement

completion_criteria.text: DOE's assessment supports the underlying validation approach through recommendations for realistic use cases, independent third-party access, lifetime testing and widely shared demonstration data. Independent evaluation and sufficiently detailed public results should allow others to assess measurement boundaries and reproduce the performance analysis. These recommendations support the method without endorsing the numerical thresholds proposed here.
completion_criteria.label: Public results enable independent evaluation and reproducible performance analysis

completion_criteria.text: Proposed interpretation: an announced factory, a modeled innovation portfolio or a pilot lacking the required measurements would not establish completion. Subsidy alone would neither validate nor invalidate technical performance; economic assessment should distinguish measured costs, financial support and assumptions about future scale. Above 95% round-trip efficiency and below $50/kWh installed may be retained as optional proposed specifications, but their historical attribution is unverified and they are not mandatory criteria here. Installed cost per unit of capacity and levelized cost per unit of delivered electricity must remain separate measures.
completion_criteria.label: Economic assessment distinguishes cost metrics, financial support and scaling assumptions

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis — PWR-01, Practical dissipationless conductors and windings for bulk power systems: lower-loss conductors and windings could complement storage by improving power transfer and conversion. Their central function concerns carrying electricity with minimal dissipation; PWR-04 concerns holding an energy inventory for later delivery. Progress in conductors would not by itself establish economical multi-day or seasonal storage.

Roster-based synthesis — PWR-02, Solid-state conversion of heat to utility electricity: this could overlap with a thermal-storage route, where stored heat must later become electricity. PWR-02 concerns the conversion step; PWR-04 additionally requires an economical reservoir, retention, charging, plant operation and system-level validation. PWR-04 could also be achieved through a storage mechanism that does not use heat-to-electricity conversion.

Roster-based synthesis — PWR-03, Utility-scale electromagnetic delivery of power without a conductor: power delivery across space could complement shifting energy across time by connecting surplus generation with demand or storage elsewhere. Delivery capability does not itself provide an energy inventory for a prolonged shortage. The two entries address distinct infrastructure functions.

Roster-based synthesis — PWR-05, An interconnection that no longer depends on synchronous machines: storage could supply energy through equipment participating in such an interconnection, but stored-energy adequacy and grid stability are separate requirements. PWR-05 addresses operation without dependence on synchronous machines; PWR-04 addresses the quantity, duration and economics of energy available for later use. Demonstrating either would not establish the other.

change_log.reason: The dated DOE assessments and empty freshness record do not support a universal absence claim as of November 1, 2026.

change_log.change: Separated discharge duration, retention and seasonal system balancing.
change_log.reason: Multi-day output and storage across weeks do not independently establish seasonal adequacy.

change_log.reason: Grids contain transient stored energy, and the original list omitted mechanisms such as flywheels.

change_log.change: Made avoided overbuilding and fossil-capacity replacement conditional on charging resources, regional reliability and economics.
change_log.reason: The storage function supports these possibilities but does not quantify or guarantee their system-level extent.

change_log.change: Distinguished DOE's 10+ hour percentage-reduction target, $0.05/kWh levelized cost target and optional installed-cost specification.
change_log.reason: These measures have different meanings and none establishes seasonal performance.

change_log.change: Corrected flow-battery projections to $0.052–$0.057/kWh and identified all innovation-portfolio outcomes as modeled.
change_log.reason: The detailed numerical result is slightly above the target despite broader summary language.

change_log.change: Qualified lithium-ion duration and chemical-carrier efficiency assertions.
change_log.reason: Typical applications do not establish a physical duration limit, and the supplied evidence does not quantify a general chemical-carrier efficiency failure.

change_log.change: Retained the attributed Form Energy test, module, deployment and project-date details with explicit verification limits.
change_log.reason: They are useful research details, but the cited page has no retained content in the supplied evidence. Their omission is unnecessary when attribution and uncertainty are preserved.

change_log.change: Expanded proposed completion criteria to include seasonal retention, auxiliary consumption, availability, material supply, independent access and regional validation.
change_log.reason: These address gaps between a successful module test and the full practical capability without presenting proposed thresholds as standards.

change_log.change: Removed subsidy status as a disqualifier and clarified the limits of one-year and finite-site demonstrations.
change_log.reason: Financial support does not determine technical validity, one year does not establish lifetime durability, and finite tests cannot prove universality.

change_log.change: Added distinct relationships to all four other roster entries.
change_log.reason: Their conductor, conversion, delivery and interconnection functions can complement storage without merging their identities.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish whether any subsequent demonstration satisfies the full combination of requirements as of November 1, 2026; the freshness record contains no search coverage.

The reported Form Energy prototype tests, test conditions, measured efficiency, module specifications, deployment progress and project conclusion remain unverified because no project-page content was retained.
The meaning and compatibility of the reported approximately 3 kW and 3,000 kWh module targets require clarification; they cannot establish tested duration on their own.
The reported December 2025 project conclusion and Active page header cannot be reconciled from the supplied evidence.
The Utility Dive article's contents and asserted publication date remain unverified. Its absence does not weaken the independently supported DOE findings.
Seasonal intervals, acceptable losses, cost boundaries and reliability requirements must be defined for an intended regional application before the proposed completion framework can be applied.
The historical attribution of above 95% round-trip efficiency and below $50/kWh installed remains unestablished; these figures are retained only as optional proposals.

The review's recommendation to remove unverified project-page assertions from the factual account was modified: the details are preserved as explicitly attributed, unverified reports to satisfy the instruction to retain useful research detail without inventing confirmation.

brief.title: Electricity stored for days and seasons
possible: Homes and businesses could use surplus wind and solar electricity through prolonged shortages and seasonal gaps. Storage could serve many regions without needing special underground formations or terrain.
why: Electricity suppliers could rely less on fossil plants held ready for shortages. Affordable reserves could also reduce the extra generating capacity needed to keep power reliable.

sources.showed: DOE set a target to cut the cost of storage that can deliver electricity for at least 10 hours. The fact sheet describes a research goal, without reporting its achievement.
sources.cited_for: Cheaper storage would let clean generation supply electricity when production falls below demand.
sources.not_established: The target does not establish affordable storage across seasonal gaps.

sources.who: U.S. Department of Energy and research partners
sources.showed: Their modeling projected that baseline storage costs would exceed DOE's target. Combinations of improvements could bring some technologies to or near it. These were cost projections for shorter uses than seasonal balancing.
sources.quote: The projected baseline 2030 LCOS of all technologies exceeds the Storage Shot target.
sources.cited_for: Cost remains a barrier; the analysis measures it as average cost per unit of electricity delivered, called levelized cost of storage.
sources.not_established: Modeled cost reductions do not demonstrate seasonal operation, and some promising options need special geology.

sources.showed: The project concerns testing an iron-air storage prototype for electricity delivery over several days.
sources.cited_for: Prototype testing addresses the multi-day delivery part of the challenge.
sources.not_established: A prototype test does not establish seasonal storage, plant durability or competitive delivered electricity costs.

shown: A California Energy Commission project account reports that a Form Energy iron-air prototype discharged for more than 100 hours in third-party testing. That would demonstrate multi-day delivery at module scale; it would leave seasonal performance and sustained plant operation unresolved.

DOE's modeling identifies ways some storage technologies could approach its cost target. It does not demonstrate an operating system combining affordable seasonal delivery with broad freedom over where it can be built.
missing: A large operating plant would need to combine multi-day delivery with acceptable losses, wear, maintenance and cost.
Stored energy would need to survive seasonal waits and supply electricity when a region actually needs it.
Materials, manufacturing and practical sites would need to support widespread deployment.

milestones.label: A large grid plant proves year-round multi-day delivery
milestones.explanation: A large grid-connected plant would have to sustain a 100-hour discharge and repeat cycles across the year, publishing losses, wear, availability, upkeep and cost. This would establish initial operating performance.

milestones.label: Stored energy covers a region's seasonal gap
milestones.explanation: A plant would have to retain energy through the required seasonal interval and deliver enough at the right time, with measured losses. This would connect storage performance to an actual regional shortage.

milestones.label: Independent analysis measures replacement of fossil backup
milestones.explanation: An independent regional study would have to use measured performance to quantify reliable fossil backup replacement, accounting for charging, weather, networks, costs, materials and sites. This would test practical system value.

milestones.label: Public results support independent performance analysis
milestones.explanation: Independent evaluators would need sufficiently detailed public results to assess what measurements include and reproduce the performance analysis. This would let others judge whether the claimed capabilities hold.

milestones.label: Economics separate measured costs from support and assumptions
milestones.explanation: An assessment would have to separate measured costs, financial support and assumptions about future scale, distinguishing construction costs from costs per unit delivered. This would make economic claims interpretable.

uncertain: Required storage intervals, acceptable losses and reliability standards depend on the region being served.
The reported prototype's measured efficiency and operating conditions remain unclear.
Seasonal storage may be used infrequently; its economics depend on affordable energy capacity and available charging electricity.

page.title: Site-independent multi-day and seasonal electricity storage
page.definition: Electricity-in/electricity-out storage without site-specific geological structures supplies multi-day shortfalls and shifts surplus energy between seasons at a cost that allows selection in a regional least-cost resource plan. Discharge duration is delivery time at specified power; seasonal retention is the interval between charging and later recovery.

goal.need: The Royal Society's Great Britain model, using 37 years of weather, shows prolonged electricity deficits when hydrogen storage capacity is reduced below that required to meet demand. DOE's August 2024 assessment projects baseline 2030 costs for all ten assessed storage technologies above its $0.05/kWh target for levelized cost of storage, the lifetime cost per unit of electricity delivered. These findings identify separate requirements for energy inventory and cost.

figures.caption: Modeled electricity shortfall with an undersized hydrogen store
figures.note: Royal Society counterfactual using 1980–2016 weather and 570 TWh/year electricity demand; storage capacity is 20% below that needed to meet demand throughout the modeled period. These are modeled shortfalls, not observed outages.

statements.quote: Wind and solar supply vary on time scales ranging from seconds to decades.

statements.body: U.S. Department of Energy, Long Duration Storage Shot
statements.quote: target to reduce the cost of grid-scale energy storage by 90% for systems that deliver 10+ hours of duration
statements.context: The reduction is relative to a 2020 lithium-ion storage baseline.

statements.body: Advanced Research Projects Agency–Energy, DAYS programme
statements.quote: The technologies in this program need to be suitable for siting throughout the entire United States.
statements.context: DAYS targets 10 to approximately 100 hours at rated power and excludes reliance on site-specific geological structures.

completion.title: A non-geological storage plant supplies multi-day and seasonal grid service in a least-cost portfolio.
completion.criterion: A full-scale system charged only by electricity, with no dependence on site-specific geological structures, supplies its contracted power and energy through both a specified multi-day shortfall and a specified seasonal surplus-to-deficit interval in grid operation. Metered charging, auxiliary consumption, retention losses, recovered electricity and availability meet the utility's predeclared acceptance requirements. Using measured performance and observed project costs, including charging, maintenance and replacement, a regional resource plan selects the system in its least-cost portfolio while meeting the region's published reliability criterion.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no combined external acceptance criterion was found.
completion.basis: DOE Storage Shot, ARPA-E DAYS, UK LoDES, Ofgem eligibility, Royal Society and EPRI reports, and the public IEC 62933-2-3 scope were searched. No joint acceptance test for non-geological siting, multi-day delivery, seasonal retention and regional economics was found in accessible text. This test uses one utility's service requirements and a regional least-cost comparison. DAYS explicitly places its 10–100-hour applications short of seasonal storage; Ofgem's eight-hour eligibility requirement also does not establish seasonal performance.

milestones.title: Electricity-storage components pass laboratory tests of application feasibility (TRL 4).
milestones.criterion: Core components or subsystems pass laboratory bench tests showing that their application performance is achievable. Thermal: SynchroStor's February 2026 report leaves its storage subsystem at technology readiness level (TRL) 4. Electrochemical: CEC's November 2025 report describes two DC iron-air modules tested in Berkeley: 117–126 hours at about 2.14 kW and 108–110 hours at about 2.81 kW. The first was retired after cycle 6; absolute round-trip efficiency is proprietary. EPRI analysed Form's test data.
milestones.set_by: UK Department for Business, Energy & Industrial Strategy, 2021 LoDES Stream 2 guidance, Appendix 1 TRL table; archived, withdrawn competition guidance.

milestones.title: An electricity-storage system passes representative full-scale prototype tests (TRL 6).
milestones.criterion: A representative full-scale prototype passes tests in conditions relevant to its intended application. Chemical: CEC's September 2025 report describes one installation with a 50-kW fuel cell, electrolyser and 18-kg hydrogen store, 13% system round-trip efficiency, and no detectable pressure loss during 12 months of tank monitoring. Thermal: SynchroStor reports TRL 6 for its compressor/expander subsystem, with further work required on the complete storage system. These component and retention results do not establish system qualification for combined multi-day and seasonal service.
milestones.set_by: UK Department for Business, Energy & Industrial Strategy, 2021 LoDES Stream 2 guidance, Appendix 1 TRL table; archived, withdrawn competition guidance.

milestones.title: An electricity-storage pilot demonstrates integrated operation at or near full scale (TRL 7).
milestones.criterion: An integrated pilot at or near intended full scale demonstrates its functions in an operational environment, including ancillary systems. Mechanical: the UK roadmap reports that Highview's 5-MW liquid-air plant, launched in 2018, supplied grid flexibility for two years. Electrochemical: Great River Energy's 2026 resource plan describes its 1.5-MW, 100-hour Cambridge iron-air project as awaiting remaining modules after structures and balance-of-plant construction were substantially complete. These accounts do not establish acceptance for combined multi-day and seasonal service.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy, Technology Readiness Levels, TRL 7 definition.
milestones.threshold_quote: System/process prototype demonstration in an operational environment

milestones.title: A full-scale electricity-storage system meets its end-user specifications in qualification tests (TRL 8).
milestones.criterion: The full-scale system is integrated into its operational environment and passes tests of all functions in simulated and operational scenarios against end-user specifications. For this capability, qualification covers multi-day delivery and seasonal retention and recovery. None of the cited results establishes this complete qualification.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy, Technology Readiness Levels, TRL 8 definition; numerical specifications belong to the intended application.
milestones.threshold_quote: All functionality is tested in simulated and operational scenarios with demonstrated achievement of end-user specifications.

results.finding: One Al-Ni molten-salt battery cell retained 92.5% of its capacity after 8 weeks.
results.detail: The cell used sulfur-doped cathode granules. It was stored at room temperature, then reheated and discharged at 3 mA. Capacity retention is not full-system energy efficiency.
results.quote:
During thermal cycling, the cell assembled with the untreated granules and 5
mol % S doping had a capacity retention of 88.8% over 1 week, 95.1% over 2 weeks,
98.3% over 4 weeks, and then 92.5% over 8 weeks ( Figure S12 ).

results.finding: One air-bridge thermophotovoltaic cell achieved 43.8% peak conversion efficiency.
results.detail: The cell was tested under 1435°C illumination. It is a potential thermal-battery component, but the study does not demonstrate an integrated storage subsystem or establish its TRL.
results.quote:
The best-performing cell is the 0.9 eV cell , which  shows a peak 
efficiency of 43.8 (±0.5) % under 1435°C illumination.

results.finding: One scaled-up Noon Energy battery demonstration reportedly provided 100+ hours of storage capacity.
results.detail: The company describes a multi-module demonstration, but does not establish that it is a representative full-scale prototype tested for combined multi-day and seasonal service. It says a larger commercial-scale system was yet to be commissioned; seasonal retention is not reported.
results.quote:
Noon Energy
has demonstrated successful long-term operation of its scaled-up ultra-long-duration energy storage (ultra-LDES) system that provides a groundbreaking 100+ hours of energy storage capacity, the missing link to clean, reliable electricity 24/7 year-round.

results.finding: AirBattery compressed-air pilot at Yahel: 1 installation achieved 47.74% calculated energy efficiency.
results.detail: An external consultant calculated efficiency from company-measured operating data and adjusted it to 45.5% when estimated frequency-converter consumption was included. The company describes Yahel as a small commercial-scale pilot; the filing does not establish full-scale qualification or multi-day and seasonal service.

results.finding: One Ore Energy iron-air pilot demonstrated 100-hour multi-day storage performance.
results.detail: The pilot operated on the grid for several months, but the source does not establish that it was at or near intended full scale or that it demonstrated ancillary systems.
results.quote:
Ore Energy has successfully concluded a grid-connected pilot of its 100-hour iron-air long-duration energy storage (LDES) system at
EDF R&D Laboratories
in Écuelles, France, demonstrating multi-day storage performance in a real utility environment.

results.finding: One HYFLEXPOWER industrial-scale pilot demonstrated integrated power-to-hydrogen-to-power operation with up to 100% hydrogen.
results.detail: The pilot integrated hydrogen conversion, compression, storage and gas-turbine re-electrification at an operating CHP plant. The report does not establish multi-day discharge or seasonal retention.
results.quote: The second campaign in 2023 demonstrated the integrated plant with the new hydrogen gas turbine technology operating with blends from 0-100% H2.

results.finding: One Al-Ni cell retained 92.3% of its capacity after 12 weeks.
results.detail: The freeze-thaw result demonstrates retention in a laboratory cell, not tests of a representative full-scale storage system.
results.quote:
Cycling at a current of 3 mA,
the cell had a capacity retention greater than 99.5% over 1 week, 98.8% over
2 weeks, greater than 99.5% over 4 weeks, 98.5% over 8 weeks, and 92.3% over
12 weeks.

results.finding: Noon Energy reports one scaled-up battery demonstration with over 200 hours of energy capacity.
results.detail: The release does not specify laboratory bench-test conditions or establish that the components passed application-feasibility tests at TRL 4.
results.quote: The reversible solid oxide fuel cell battery is the first fully containerized, modular ultra-LDES system successfully operated for thousands of hours, with storage of over 200 hours of energy capacity, marking an incredible milestone in the energy industry.

results.finding: Noon Energy reports one multi-module demonstration system operated for thousands of hours.
results.detail: The release does not establish operation at or near intended full scale in an operational environment, including ancillary systems. It says a larger commercial-scale system is yet to be commissioned.
results.quote: We are excited to have commissioned our multi-module demonstration system and demonstrated its lifetime, thanks to the excellent work of our incredible engineering team.

results.finding: One grid-connected 100-hour iron-air storage pilot operated for several months.
results.detail: The pilot operated under real-world grid conditions, but the source does not establish that it was full-scale or report a measured 100-hour discharge test.
results.quote: Supported by the EU’s Storage Research Infrastructure Eco-System (StoRIES) programme, the modular system operated under real-world grid conditions for several months, collecting operational data on charge/discharge behavior and grid integration.

results.finding: One integrated industrial power-to-hydrogen-to-power plant operated for more than 10 hours above 80% hydrogen.
results.detail: The plant was demonstrated in an operating industrial facility, but the report does not establish multi-day delivery or seasonal storage and recovery.
results.quote: The testing campaign achieved the objectives of more than 10 hours operation above 80% H2 with less than 25 ppm NOx emissions.

results.finding: Al-Ni freeze-thaw cell, sample size not stated: capacity retained after more than 18 months.
results.detail: The presentation reports 98.4% capacity retention for an Al-Ni cell with 5% sulfur. It does not state the sample size or report system-level round-trip efficiency.
results.quote:
Continued testing for longer durations shows 
excellent capacity retention for > 18 months:

results.finding: Chemical storage: one laboratory-scale pilot reactor stored 7.1 kg of hydrogen over two successful cycles.
results.detail: The 210 L steam-iron reactor demonstrates a chemical-storage subsystem. The presentation does not report electricity-to-electricity performance.
results.quote:
Reactor of 210 L size [1-3] 
2 successful cycles shown 
7.1 kg H2 stored

results.finding: One CHESTER thermal storage laboratory prototype demonstrated stable integrated operation at a 10 kW scale.
results.detail: The prototype combined a heat pump, thermal storage and an organic Rankine cycle. The reported discharge experiment used preconditioned storage and an external heat source.
results.quote:
The stable operation of a fully integrated CHEST system on a 10 kW scale was demonstrated and the stable function of 
the latent heat storage unit as both a condenser and an evaporator was confirmed.

results.finding: One SustainX compressed-air storage prototype operated at commercial scale, rated at 1.5 MW.
results.detail: The prototype operated in charge and discharge modes, but the supplied text does not establish that it passed tests for combined multi-day and seasonal service.
results.quote: The 1.5 MW Commercial Prototype has been operational for both compressions (charge) and expansions (discharge) since September 30, 2013.

results.finding: One integrated Greek hydrogen-storage pilot had a 50-kW fuel cell.
results.detail: The source reports efficiency results for the integrated microgrid pilot, but does not establish that it operated at or near its intended full scale or demonstrate all ancillary functions.
results.quote:

Micro-grid
